newsitem.title: IRAN: Outgoing energy minister named Iran oil minister.
newsitem.headline: Outgoing energy minister named Iran oil minister.

text.p: Bijan Namdar Zanganeh, nominated by Iranian President Mohammad Khatami on Tuesday to head the oil ministry, is the Islamic republic's outgoing energy minister and has held senior government posts for more than 10 years.

If confirmed by Iran's parliament, or Majlis, Zanganeh would replace veteran oil minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh at the helm of the powerful ministry in the world's third largest oil exporting country after Saudi Arabia and Norway.
Iran, which has a crude oil output of 3.6 million barrels a day, is the second largest producer in the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).
Forty percent of government revenues come from oil.
Aghazadeh is expected to retain an important position in a mediating council headed by outgoing president Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.
As energy minister Zanganeh oversaw Iran's domestic power and its non-oil energy sector.

During his term, he said Iran had achieved self-sufficiency in building dams and manufacturing electricity facilities. He also called for significant cuts in energy consumption to save the country more than $5 billion a year.
Zanganeh, who was born in 1952 in the western province of Kermanshahan, has a master's degree in civil engineering from Tehran University. He is widely seen as a technocrat.
After the 1979 Islamic revolution, he worked as a university lecturer and served as deputy culture and Islamic guidance minister before being appointed to head the construction ministry in 1984.
He resigned from the post in 1988 and became energy minister following a minor cabinet reshuffle the same year.
